note: Conversion-first creative briefs. These are not publishable until a visual is produced and explicitly approved. They exist to stop the autoposter from drifting back into generic educational content.

briefs.buyer: premium product brand planning a launch
briefs.support: Let people inspect, reveal, and understand it while they scroll.
briefs.visual_concept: A premium physical product isolated in a dark studio. Three exploded states of the same object float along one scroll path, connected by a precise orange motion line. No browser chrome. The product is the dominant visual.

briefs.hook: A LAUNCH SHOULD FEEL LIKE A REVEAL.
briefs.support: Build anticipation, show the detail, then make the next step obvious.
briefs.visual_concept: One object moves from silhouette to partially revealed to fully lit. The states overlap like one continuous cinematic sequence. The composition feels like a campaign still, not a website screenshot.

briefs.buyer: company selling a product that needs explanation
briefs.support: Turn features into something the buyer can explore.
briefs.visual_concept: A product cross-section with three labeled interactive hotspots and one visible cursor path. The product occupies more than half the frame. Copy remains secondary.

briefs.buyer: brand with a high-value launch using a conventional landing page
briefs.hook: YOUR PRODUCT MOVES. YOUR SITE SHOULD TOO.
briefs.support: Make the launch behave like the thing you're selling.
briefs.visual_concept: Hard visual contrast: left side a flat static card, right side the same product breaking out into layered depth and motion. The right side must feel materially richer, not merely brighter.

briefs.buyer: brand that needs a cinematic story rather than a brochure site
briefs.support: One continuous sequence from first frame to final action.
briefs.visual_concept: A vertical narrative path with four cinematic frames of one hero object changing state. Frames are connected physically, not arranged as a generic four-card grid.

briefs.buyer: premium brand whose current website undersells the product
briefs.hook: PREMIUM SHOULD BE FELT BEFORE IT'S READ.
briefs.support: Interaction, pacing, and detail make the first impression do the selling.
briefs.visual_concept: Editorial macro product detail with a controlled cursor-reveal window exposing hidden material or internal structure. No generic luxury gradients.

briefs.hook: BUILT AROUND THE PRODUCT. NOT A TEMPLATE.
briefs.support: Story, interaction, motion, and responsive behavior designed together.
briefs.visual_concept: One final polished screen sits above a stripped-back system layer showing motion path, interaction states, type scale, and responsive frames. It should look like evidence from a real design process, not a moodboard.

briefs.buyer: brand selling a product where construction or material quality matters
briefs.hook: SHOW THE DETAIL THEY'RE PAYING FOR.
briefs.support: Use interaction to reveal construction, materials, and function.
briefs.visual_concept: Macro component detail expands into a clean exploded view. One orange annotation line identifies a meaningful feature. The object, not the copy, carries the frame.
